We have template info. The mapped_rxn is given: 'Cl[CH2:10][Cl:11].[F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][c:9]([CH2:10][Cl:11])[cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH2:14]1>>[F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][c:9]([CH2:10][Cl:11])[cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH2:14]1'

So product is the right side: [F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][c:9]([CH2:10][Cl:11])[cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH2:14]1

We need to apply the template to that product to get precursors. Use apply_template tool with molecule_smiles = product SMILES (need to convert to normal SMILES). The mapped product SMILES includes atom mapping numbers but should be acceptable? Usually apply_template expects normal SMILES. We can strip mapping numbers. The product SMILES: [F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][c:9]([CH2:10][Cl:11])[cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH2:14]1

Remove atom map tags like :1 etc. So product SMILES: F[C]1CCN(CCc2ccc(Cl)cc2)C1? Wait need to interpret.

Let's decode: [F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][c:9]([CH2:10][Cl:11])[cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH2:14]1

Simplify: F-CH- (CH?) Actually [CH:2]1 indicates a carbon with H attached, part of ring. So it's a fluorinated cyclized amine with aromatic substituent.

Probably the product SMILES is "FC1CCN(CCc2ccc(Cl)cc2)C1". Let's verify: The aromatic part: [c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][c:9]([CH2:10][Cl:11])[cH:12][cH:13]2 corresponds to a phenyl ring with a CH2Cl substituent at position 3? Actually c9 attached to CH2Cl. So aromatic ring: c1c c c(cCl) c c1 (with CH2 attached to N). So overall: N attached to CH2 (position 5) which attaches to aromatic carbon (c6) which is part of phenyl ring with CH2Cl substituent.

Thus product SMILES: FC1CCN(CCc2ccc(Cl)cc2)C1. That matches typical structure: a fluorinated piperidine? Actually C1CCN... ring is a morpholine? Let's trust.

Now apply template. Use apply_template with product SMILES and template_id 1914394.
